worksheet.title: Which Way?
worksheet.subtitle: Choose the arrow that goes to the star
worksheet.learning_goal: I can choose the arrow that moves Bit toward the star.

parts.title: Pick the right direction
parts.text: ➡ moves Bit to the right. ⬅ moves Bit to the left. Look at where the star is, then pick the arrow that moves Bit toward it.

parts.title: Watch Bit — star is to the right
parts.note: The star (box 5) is to the RIGHT of Bit (box 3). So Bit should go ➡.

parts.title: Bit on box 2, star on box 5
parts.prompt: Which arrow moves Bit toward the star? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: Bit on box 4, star on box 2
parts.prompt: The star is to the LEFT this time. Which arrow moves Bit toward it? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: You try — Bit on box 5, star on box 1
parts.prompt: Which arrow moves Bit toward the star? Circle it.    ➡    ⬅

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Choosing the right direction is part of making a plan. The first thing a coder asks is: which way do I need to go?

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children choose the single arrow (➡ or ⬅) that moves Bit toward the star. Selecting the correct direction toward a goal is the first planning decision in building an algorithm.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children use directional language and choose a direction toward a goal.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles ➡ or ⬅.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: floor boxes with Bit and a star to point the way by hand.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: 'The star is on box 5, Bit is on box 3. Box 5 is to the right, so Bit goes ➡.'
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — star to the right → ➡.
3. YOU TRY: children pick ⬅ when the star is to the left (Ex 2 and Ex 3).
4. Connect: 'A coder first asks: which way do I need to go?'

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: always choosing ➡ — have them point from Bit to the star first to feel the direction.
Simplify: use only box positions next to each other (Bit on 2, star on 3).
Extend: ask how many steps in that direction reach the star.
Movement option: stand a child as Bit and place a star; the class calls 'left' or 'right'.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child circles the arrow pointing toward the star in every case, including when the star is to the left.
